newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices end flat to softer.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices end flat to softer.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds ended flat to down 1/8 point in lackluster trade ahead of Wednesday's September Consumer Price Index report.
"I think the market is a little nervous, but I think (CPI) should come in in the consensus," one trader said. "I don't think it's a problem."
Economists polled by Reuters expect a 0.3 percent rise both overall and in the core rate, which excludes the more volatile food and energy prices.
Data aside, buying interest in munis remains thin, with several factors conspiring to squelch interest, a trader said. He judged muni cash down 1/8 point overall Tuesday.
"I think they got to a point where people thought they were a little rich," he said, adding that, "I think that there's a little bit of a calendar building up."
In addition, mutual funds apparently "got where they had to be before quarter end," and felt little additional pressure to act.
"So as a result they are going to be a little more selective, and they are willing to wait," he said. "They lost about $700 million last week also."
Another market source said outflows from municipal bond funds was about $669 millon in the latest reporting week.

As for retail, "customers are preoccupied with other places to put their money." The stock market, where the Dow Jones Industrial Average held above the 6,000 level at the close, is one obvious lure, the trader said.

A municipal analyst said the overall municipal market ended unchanged to slightly weaker. High-grade issues closed unchanged, while dollar bonds closed "down a couple of ticks." Secondary activity was light, he said.
In debt futures, the December municipal contract closed down 8/32 at 114-14/32. The December T-bond contract closed down 3/32 at 110-16/32. The MOB spread was 126 ticks.
In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed up 1/32 at 98-26/32 to yield 6.84 percent.

As for new issues, pricing was firm, the analyst said. Lehman Brothers won $165 million Airports Commission of the City and County of San Francisco, Calif., alternative minimum tax bonds at a true interest cost of 5.933 percent. The top maturity in 2026 was had a 5.9 percent coupon and a dollar price of 97.
First Albany said it won $110 million of non-AMT San Francisco Airport bonds at a 5.7321 percent TIC. The offering featured a top yield of 5.730 percent in 2026.
On the negotiated side, JP Morgan Securities Inc tentatively priced $79.8 million Connecticut refunding bonds at a top yield of 5.30 percent in 2009.
EVEREN Securities Inc said it repriced DeWitt Public Schools, Michigan's $39.5 million bond offering, raising yields in several maturities, but leaving the top yield in 2026 unchanged.

Looking ahead, the New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority said it has delayed its $371 million bond sale from Wednesday until at least Thursday. The city is expected to make an announcement Wednesday regarding the sale. The delay is linked to the agency's annual audit, a city official said.
